_strings.@@37d4d0c249ef: Sales Tax Relief Credit (Sales Tax Refund) — Must be an Oklahoma resident for the entire year. General limit is $20,000 of total gross household income, raised to $50,000 if any one of the following applies: you can claim an exemption for your dependent; you are 65 years of age or older by December 31, 2025; or you have a physical disability constituting a substantial handicap to employment (proof required, see Form 538-S). Excluded: anyone who received TANF for any month of 2025; a person convicted of a felony who was a Department of Corrections inmate for any part of the year. _strings.@@c58c9a6196a6: Oklahoma Earned Income Credit (EIC) — Resident and part-year resident filers who qualify for the federal Earned Income Credit. The federal EIC is recalculated using the federal EITC eligibility/computation requirements in effect for the 2020 tax year. A copy of the federal return and OTC Form 511-EIC must be provided.
_strings.@@d4abf582158e: Treaty conformity — OK conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OK income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OK return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Oklahoma's resident return (Form 511) starts at line 1 from "Federal adjusted gross income (from Federal 1040 or 1040-SR)" and then applies Schedule 511-A (Oklahoma subtractions) and Schedule 511-B (Oklahoma additions) to arrive at Oklahoma AGI on line 7. The complete Schedule 511-B additions list for 2025 is closed and enumerated (lines 1-9, totalled on line 10 and carried to Form 511 line 6): (1) state and municipal bond interest, (2) out-of-state losses, (3) lump-sum distributions not included in federal AGI, (4) federal net operating loss, (5) recapture of depletion claimed on a lease bonus / add-back of excess federal depletion, (6) recapture of Oklahoma 529 and OklahomaDream 529 contributions, (7) Oklahoma loss distributed by an electing PTE, (8) Oklahoma bonus depreciation add-back, (9) miscellaneous other additions. There is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income anywhere in the 2025 resident packet (a full-text search of the packet for "treaty"/"treaties" returns zero hits). Because OK begins from federal AGI and does not add treaty income back (unlike CA Schedule CA), federally treaty-exempt income already excluded from federal AGI flows through and is NOT re-taxed by Oklahoma. Therefore conforms = true. (Same analysis and result as 2023 and 2024.)

Second pass: the bracket-by-bracket schedule verified verbatim against 68 O.S. Section 2355(C) as amended by 2025 House Bill 2764 (ENROLLED text, oklegislature.gov), which retitles subsection C to 'tax years 2024 and 2025' and leaves the six brackets and the 4.75% top rate unchanged, while its NEW subsection D (three brackets, 4.5% top rate) applies only 'For tax year 2026 and for subsequent tax years'. Both passes agree, and printed table rows corroborate every boundary (e.g. the 12,300-12,350 row reads $397 Single / $229 MFJ, and the 16,300-16,350 row $587 / $398 — matching the MFJ 3.75% band that ends at $14,400).

Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,000 — 'Special' additional $1,000 exemption per taxpayer or spouse who is 65 years of age or older at the close of the tax year, allowed ONLY if Form 511 line 1 Federal AGI does not exceed $15,000 single / $25,000 joint / $12,500 married filing separate / $19,000 head of household (2025 packet, Top of Form Instructions F EXEMPTIONS — income from a traditional-IRA-to-Roth conversion is excluded in applying these limits, with Form 8606 attached). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — if eligible, claim it in the exemption boxes at the top of Form 511 and it flows into line 11.); blind ($1,000 — Additional $1,000 exemption per taxpayer or spouse who is legally blind; part of the top-of-form exemption count flowing into Form 511 line 11. NOT applied by calc.state_tax — claim it on the form.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: NO 2025 RATE CHANGE — and the widely-cited Oklahoma rate cut is a 2026 event: 2025 House Bill 2764 (signed May 28, 2025) amended 68 O.S. Section 2355 so that subsection C now reads 'For all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024 tax years 2024 and 2025' — the six-bracket 0.25%/0.75%/1.75%/2.75%/3.75%/4.75% schedule shipped here is unchanged from TY2024, top rate still 4.75%. HB 2764's NEW subsection D applies 'For tax year 2026 and for subsequent tax years': Single/MFS 0% on the first $3,750, 2.5% on the next $1,150, 3.5% on the next $2,300, 4.5% on the remainder; MFJ/surviving spouse/HOH 0% on the first $7,500, 2.5% on the next $2,300, 3.5% on the next $4,600, 4.5% on the remainder — with subsection E allowing further 0.25-point reductions on a State Board of Equalization revenue trigger. Do NOT use subsection D for 2025. The standard deductions ($6,350/$12,700/$9,350), the $1,000 exemptions, and the packet's $100,000+ worksheet constants ($4,562/$4,373) are likewise identical to 2024. Base guidance: supply 2025 Form 511, line 9 'Oklahoma income after adjustments (line 7 minus line 8)'. Line 1 starts from federal AGI; lines 2-8 apply Oklahoma subtractions (Schedule 511-A), out-of-state income (line 4), Oklahoma additions (Schedule 511-B, lines 1-9 totalled on line 10) and Oklahoma adjustments (Schedule 511-C) to reach line 9. The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Form 511 line 10) and $1,000 per exemption/dependent (Form 511 line 11) to reproduce line 13 'Oklahoma Taxable Income', and applies the brackets to reproduce line 14a. Do NOT pre-subtract deductions or exemptions from the figure you supply. If Form 511 line 4 (out-of-state income) is more than zero, or you itemize, the shipped fixed deduction/exemption amounts do not apply — see the notes below. Tax Table mandate below $100,000: Form 511 line 14a instructs 'Oklahoma Income Tax from Tax Table (see pages 27-38 of instructions)'. The 2025 table's $50-wide bands compute tax at the band midpoint, so plain bracket math may differ from the filed table figure by a few dollars within a band. The filed form must use the table below $100,000. Oklahoma also mandates whole-dollar rounding with cents included until the final total ('Drop amounts under 50 cents to the lower dollar and round amounts from 50 to 99 cents up to the next dollar'), which is exactly this engine's half-up rule. Taxable income of $100,000 or more uses the packet's tax computation worksheets (p. 38): Single/Married Filing Separate tax = $4,562 plus 0.0475 of the excess over $100,000; Married Filing Joint/Head of Household/Qualified Widow(er) tax = $4,373 plus 0.0475 of the excess over $100,000. The footnote '* This column must also be used by a Qualified Surviving Spouse' applies to the MFJ worksheet and table column. Printed worksheet constants vs exact bracket sums (re-derived for 2025): the MFJ/HOH/QW constant $4,373 exactly equals the cumulative bracket sum at $100,000 ($307.00 through $14,400 plus 4.75% x $85,600 = $4,066); the Single/MFS constant $4,562 is the exact cumulative sum $4,561.50 rounded up $0.50 ($153.50 through $7,200 plus 4.75% x $92,800 = $4,408), so above $100,000 the Single/MFS form worksheet can come out $1 higher than exact marginal bracket math after whole-dollar rounding. Bracket schedule source: the 2025 Form 511 packet prints only the Tax Table and the $100,000+ worksheets, not a marginal rate schedule. The brackets shipped here are copied verbatim from 68 O.S. Section 2355(C) as amended by 2025 HB 2764 (enrolled text on oklegislature.gov, a .gov host — an improvement over the 2024 pack, which had to read the same subsection on the non-gov OSCN statute site), and every boundary was cross-checked against the packet's printed table rows and worksheet constants. One schedule covers Single and Married Filing Separately (identical thresholds — 68 O.S. Section 2355(C)(1)); a second schedule covers Married Filing Jointly, surviving spouse, AND Head of Household (Section 2355(C)(2)) — HOH is NOT a separate schedule, it is duplicated from MFJ here. The 2025 tax table likewise has only two columns: 'Single or married filing separate' and 'Married filing joint or head of household'. Qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column and schedule (2025 tax table/worksheet footnote 'This column must also be used by a Qualified Surviving Spouse'; the statute includes surviving spouses in the MFJ paragraph; the line 10 instructions give a qualifying surviving spouse the $12,700 standard deduction) — the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping is correct for Oklahoma. Out-of-state income gate: 'STOP AND READ: If line 4 on page 1 is zero, complete lines 10-11. If line 4 is more than zero, see Schedule 511-E and do not complete lines 10-11.' When Form 511 line 4 (out-of-state income other than wages) is more than zero, Schedule 511-E prorates deductions and exemptions, so the fixed standard deduction and $1,000 exemptions shipped here do NOT apply — compute them on the form and supply a base that already reflects Schedule 511-E line 5. Itemizers: if you claimed itemized deductions on your federal return you MUST claim Oklahoma itemized deductions (Schedule 511-D) instead of the standard deduction; state and local sales or income tax from federal Schedule A must be added back, and Oklahoma itemized deductions are limited to $17,000 (charitable contributions and medical expenses are not subject to the $17,000 limit). For an itemizer, do not use the shipped standard_deduction — compute line 10 from Schedule 511-D on the form. Not modeled here: line 14(b) the additional 10% Health Savings Account tax, Farm Income Averaging (Form 573), the credit for tax paid to another state (Form 511-TX, line 16), Form 511-CR other credits (which for 2025 newly include the Electric Vehicle Charging Tax Credit), and every refundable/nonrefundable credit in the pack's credits block — all sit outside the rate schedule.
